text:
Maya: quick brain-dump — what if we add a tiny 'preflight' step that runs before any bench to catch obvious incompatibilities (tokenizer, ABI, kv-cache shapes) so we don't waste a full smoke run?
Liam: sounds sensible. whats the minimum we need to make it worthwhile?
Sofia: minimum useful set = tokenizer id probe (a few canonical strings), kv-cache shape/dtype check, and a micro-forward (1 sequence) to confirm output shape + small numeric sanity.
Maya: target: keep preflight under ~1s on a warmed worker. token-probe + micro-forward -> only enqueue bench if pass.
Liam: how do we report failures? a boolean is too blunt. structured reasons + tiny evidence so we can chart flaky patterns.
Sofia: agree. propose a compact schema saved in metadata: [reason_code, component, evidence_snippet] — e.g. TOKENIZER_MAP | tokenizer | "token id 512 != expected 513". short strings only.
Alex: caveat — micro-forward depends on kernel selection & link-time kernels. running preflight on a host with different kernels than prod serving could yield false positives. for Dedicated/Private run in the real sandbox; for hosted maybe run a kernel-fingerprint check instead of full forward.
Priya: ops note: gate must be versioned. we need gate_version in intake record so results are reproducible as policies change. semver the gate logic.
DevOpsBot: note: preflight-v1 image scheduled on intake-workers pool: ml-sandbox:v2026-08-01.
Liam: also pin tokenizer-spec-version and opset-map-hash in the intake record.
Maya: UX: intake API should return an early verdict object: {status: "accepted"|"queued", preflight: {state: "pass"|"fail", reasons: [...], gate_version: "1.0.0"}}. keep payload tiny.
Sofia: numeric tolerance question for quantized binaries — small numeric deltas across hardware are expected. add tolerance enum: strict/medium/lenient in intake.yaml. default=medium.
Alex: implementation sketch:
1) token_probe (stateless checks against canonical strings)
2) micro-forward with deterministic RNG + compare to golden tensor (relative L2 threshold)
3) short-circuit to fail if checks fail
Sofia: pseudo snippet:
```
seed = 2026
x = randint(seed, (1,16))
out = model.forward(x)
if l2(out, golden)/norm(golden) > REL_THRESH:
  fail("GOLDEN_MISMATCH")
```
Liam: where to store golden artifacts? tiny immutable blobs in blobstore keyed by model-family + gate_version; use content-hash and readonly ACL. updates only via gated process.
Priya: telemetry: metric.entry_preflight_fail_rate (1m/5m). create dashboard and alert if >3 fails/hour.
DevOpsBot: metric created: metric.entry_preflight_fail_rate (1m,5m). alert rule: >3 in 1h.
Maya: security: do not log model weights or full tensors. logs should contain only hashes, small evidence strings, gate_version. redact everything else.
Alex: rollout plan: alpha internal models (1 week), opt-in beta for some hosted customers, then default for new intakes with an opt-out flag.
Liam: docs: short playbook + common tokenizer remediation steps. I'll draft a doc and sample curl responses.
Sofia: I'll prototype micro-runner + golden compare; will test on amd64 + nvidia images and post results (PR by Friday).
Priya: ops items: gate-versioning API, blobstore path for goldens, metrics & dashboard.
Maya: action items:
- Liam: docs + failure schema (due Wed EOD)
- Sofia: prototype runner + tests (PR Fri)
- Alex: tolerance semantics for quantized models (sync Thu)
- Priya/Ops: setup gate-versioning + metrics + blobstore policy
Maya: thanks all — tagging @Liam @Sofia. :thumbsup:
Liam: noted, will post PR link when ready.
Sofia: will include test matrix (cpu/gpu) and expected runtimes.
Alex: small extra: allow manual re-run of preflight from console after minor fixes.
Maya: yes, re-run button in console + link to evidence.
DevOpsBot: reminder: intake-workers maintenance scheduled tomorrow 02:00-03:00 UTC.
Maya: OK, avoid heavy canary runs in that window.
Liam: one more: include gate_version in the model audit log so we can retroactively explain failures.
Maya: done. good catch.
Sofia: will ensure tests emit concise evidence only.
Priya: ops will ensure access control on golden blob updates. gate updates require 2 approvals.
Maya: perfect. closing thread.
